legs.label: Troy → the Cicones at Ismarus
legs.note: A real Thracian people; the raid costs six men from each ship.

legs.label: Ismarus → Cape Malea
legs.note: The last securely known point. From here a north wind drives the fleet into unknown seas for nine days.

legs.label: Malea → the Lotus-Eaters
legs.note: Ancient writers placed them in North Africa (Djerba); the poem gives no geography.

legs.label: Lotus-Eaters → land of the Cyclopes
legs.note: Sicily near Etna is the classic identification (Thucydides reports it as tradition).

legs.label: Cyclopes → Aeolus' island
legs.note: Named the Aeolian Islands in antiquity. In the poem the released winds blow them almost to Ithaca and back again.

legs.label: Aeolia → the Laestrygonians
legs.note: Competing identifications (Sicily, Formiae, Bonifacio). Eleven of twelve ships are lost.

legs.label: Laestrygonians → Circe's Aeaea
legs.note: The poem locates Aeaea in the east, by the house of Dawn; ancient Italians pointed to Monte Circeo. Shown on the symbolic map.

legs.label: Aeaea → the edge of Ocean and the dead
legs.note: Odysseus sails to the streams of Ocean to consult Tiresias. Later writers linked the scene with Lake Avernus or the Acheron — those are receptions, not the poem's geography.

legs.label: Return to Aeaea
legs.note: They return to Circe to bury Elpenor and receive directions.

legs.label: Aeaea → the Sirens
legs.note: Strabo knew islets off Sorrento as the Sirenussae.

legs.label: Sirens → Scylla and Charybdis
legs.note: The Strait of Messina, identified since Thucydides — the firmest identification of the wanderings.

legs.label: → Thrinacia, the Sun's cattle
legs.note: Equated with Sicily (Trinacria). The crew eat the cattle and Zeus destroys the ship.

legs.label: Shipwreck → Calypso's Ogygia
legs.note: Odysseus drifts nine days, back past Charybdis, to Ogygia, 'the navel of the sea'. He stays seven years.

legs.label: Ogygia → Scheria of the Phaeacians
legs.note: Seventeen days on a raft, then Poseidon's storm. Scheria was identified with Corfu in antiquity.

legs.label: Scheria → home to Ithaca
legs.note: Carried home asleep by a Phaeacian ship. Modern Ithaki is the traditional island; Kefalonia's Paliki peninsula is a modern alternative.
